    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Representation.FiniteDimensional, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Finite-dimensional quiver representations #

    A representation of a quiver is pointwise finite-dimensional when the vector space it puts at every vertex is finite-dimensional. This file defines that property, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.IsFinDim, proves that it is stable under subobjects and quotients, equips its full subcategory with an abelian structure and an exact inclusion, proves essential smallness for a finite vertex set, and shows that a path algebra module finite-dimensional over the base field gives such a representation.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.IsFinDim: a representation is finite-dimensional at every vertex.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.IsFinDim.of_iso: pointwise finite-dimensionality transports along an isomorphism.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.IsFinDim.of_mono and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.IsFinDim.of_epi: subobjects and quotients of pointwise finite-dimensional representations are pointwise finite-dimensional.
    • The full subcategory of IsFinDim representations is abelian, by Mathlib's abelian full-subcategory construction. Its inclusion preserves finite limits and colimits, so kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences have their ambient pointwise meaning.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.isFinDim_biproduct: finite biproducts of finite-dimensional representations are finite-dimensional.
    • The full subcategory of IsFinDim representations is essentially small for finite Q.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.module_finite_asModule_of_isFinDim: a pointwise finite-dimensional representation gives a finite module over the path algebra when the vertex set is finite.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.module_finite_quiverRepEquivalenceFunctorObj_of_isFinDim: the module it is carried to by LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalence is finite-dimensional over the base field.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.isFinDim_quiverRepFunctor_obj: finite-dimensionality passes from a module to its associated representation.

    Implementation notes #

    IsFinDim is stated vertex by vertex rather than as a single finiteness of the total space: the category of representations is a functor category, with no ambient module to be finite over, and over an infinite vertex set the two conditions genuinely differ. Over a finite quiver they agree, and that is the setting the theory is meant for.

    source
    def LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.IsFinDim (k : Type u) (Q : Type v) [Field k] [Quiver Q] (M : QuiverRep k Q) :
    Prop

    Pointwise finite-dimensionality of a quiver representation: the vector space at every vertex is finite-dimensional. Over a finite quiver this is total finite-dimensionality, and it is the finiteness condition under which the indecomposables can be counted; the functor category itself contains infinite-dimensional objects.

      theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.IsFinDim.of_mono {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] {M N : QuiverRep k Q} (hM : IsFinDim k Q M) (f : N ⟶ M) [CategoryTheory.Mono f] :

      A subobject of a pointwise finite-dimensional representation is pointwise finite-dimensional. A monomorphism of representations is a monomorphism at every vertex, hence an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space. The intended instance is a biproduct summand, CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι being a split monomorphism.

        instance LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.instFiniteAsModuleOfVertexSpace (k : Type u) (Q : Type v) [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Finite Q] [DecidableEq Q] (M : QuiverRep k Q) [∀ (i : Q), Module.Finite k (QuiverRep.vertexSpace k Q M i)] :

        Over a finite quiver, the module carried by a representation with finite-dimensional vertex spaces is finite-dimensional, being the direct sum of those spaces. This is the quiver counterpart of Mathlib's instance Module.Finite k ρ.asModule for Representation.asModule.

        theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.module_finite_quiverRepEquivalenceFunctorObj_of_isFinDim (k : Type u) (Q : Type v) [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Finite Q] (M : QuiverRep k Q) (hM : IsFinDim k Q M) :
        Module.Finite k ↑((quiverRepEquivalence k Q).functor.obj M)

        A pointwise finite-dimensional representation of a finite quiver is carried to a finite-dimensional module by LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalence. That module is the direct sum of the vertex spaces, so finite-dimensionality at every vertex is finite-dimensionality of the module. Finite-dimensionality over k is what makes the module Artinian and Noetherian over kQ, by isArtinian_of_tower and isNoetherian_of_tower, and so is the route by which a theorem about modules of finite length reaches a finite-dimensional representation.

        Module.Finite (pathAlgebra k Q) ↑((quiverRepEquivalence k Q).functor.obj M)

        The path-algebra module of a pointwise finite-dimensional representation is finitely generated over the path algebra, being finite-dimensional over the ground field.
